standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard: an abelian sheaf is a sheaf of sets equipped with a commutative group law, and a module over G is a G-set equipped with a commutative group law
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reason the equivalence restricts to abelian objects.

core_obligations: Recall the set-theoretic equivalence (proof lines 9091-9093): the theorem already quoted gives an equivalence between sheaves of sets on the small etale site of Spec(K) and sets with an action of the absolute Galois group.

Transport the commutative group law (proof lines 9094-9096): an abelian sheaf is a sheaf of sets endowed with a commutative group law and a module over G is a G-set endowed with a commutative group law, so the equivalence restricts to the categories of abelian objects.
proof_roadmap: Invoke the equivalence between sheaves of sets and Galois sets at the chosen geometric point.
Observe that both sides are the categories of commutative group objects in the two equivalent categories.
Conclude that the stalk functor is an equivalence of the abelian categories.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for S = Spec(K) with K a field and a geometric point fixed, the stalk functor is an equivalence between abelian sheaves on S_etale and modules over the absolute Galois group (statement lines 9077-9088). The proof is a short but complete formal transport: the equivalence between sheaves of sets and Galois sets is already available (proof lines 9091-9093), and the author explains that an abelian sheaf is precisely a sheaf of sets with a commutative group law while a Galois module is precisely a Galois set with a commutative group law, so the equivalence restricts (proof lines 9094-9096). The non-formal content is the recognition that both sides are categories of commutative group objects. The claim is H1: a one-step formal transport whose reason is written out.
